name: uri-non-numeric-port-invalid
description: permittedSubtrees uniformResourceIdentifier is 'example.com'. The leaf's URI SAN is 'foo://example.com:a443/path' — the port component contains a letter. Per RFC 3986 ABNF, port = *DIGIT, so the URI is syntactically malformed and must be rejected. A validator that splits at the first ':' to extract the host could mishandle the trailing 'a443' in surprising ways depending on how greedy the split is.
references: BoringSSL b84dc606 — crypto/x509: Tighten URI name constraints parsing and matching
notes: BoringSSL post-b84dc606 explicitly added this case to its name-constraint test suite. Pre-fix behaviour varies: implementations that don't validate the port component may extract the host as 'example.com' and accept (matching the constraint); strict parsers reject the URI outright.
